claim: zip(columns, rows[0], strict=True) never raises: the single payload row always has exactly len(columns) cells (including when DataFrameComponent rows lack a key or columns are explicitly given)
evidence: In _compute_table_payload (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:901-908), coerced_rows are built as `[[_coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) for c in columns] for row in rows]` — each row list is always exactly len(columns) long because it iterates over `columns` and uses `.get(c, "")` with a default, so a missing key in a DataFrameComponent row dict just yields an empty-string cell rather than a short list. This payload flows unchanged into _small_result_to_markdown (line 1200), where `columns = payload.get('columns')` and `rows = payload.get('rows')` are the same lists, so `zip(columns, rows[0], strict=True)` at line 1219 always zips two equal-length sequences and cannot raise ValueError regardless of whether the original rows lacked keys or columns were explicitly supplied.

claim: The widget's markdown-it renderer (html:false) renders backslash-escaped **col:** value lines as literal text (escapes honored, backslash not shown)
evidence: src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1192-1219 builds `**col:** value` lines via _escape_small_result_text, which backslash-escapes CommonMark punctuation (_SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = \`*_[]<>~|&, line 49) before rendering. src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html:753 constructs the renderer with markdownit({ html: false, ... }); the `html` option only controls whether raw HTML in the source is passed through vs. escaped (comment at lines 744-747 confirms: 'html: false -> raw HTML in the text is escaped, never passed through'). claim: The comment says the escaping makes database values render as literal text rather than Markdown formatting. Test whether any value can still produce formatting.

verify_hint: Falsifying values: '# heading', '1. item', '- x', '> ', autolinks with linkify, '!', '(', entities; check markdown-it/GFM
evidence: src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:49 defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&"). _escape_small_result_text (line 1192-1197) only prepends a backslash before these specific characters; any other character, including a bare URL such as 'http://example.com' or 'www.example.com', is left completely untouched (no '\\', ':' or '.' in the escaped set). GFM-style Markdown renderers with linkify enabled (a common MCP-client rendering mode, and the exact scenario named in the item's verify_hint) will still autolink such a value into a clickable link, i.e. Markdown formatting, even though it contains none of the backslash-escaped characters. Therefore the comment's claim that escaping these characters makes database values 'render as literal text rather than Markdown formatting' is not universally true — it is falsified by bare-URL/autolink values.

claim: tools.md says line breaks are flattened. Test whether the code flattens every line break.
source_excerpt: with column names and values backslash-escaped for Markdown syntax and line breaks flattened
evidence: docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md:96 says values are rendered 'with column names and values backslash-escaped for Markdown syntax and line breaks flattened'. The implementation, _escape_small_result_text at src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1192-1197, only does value.replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ") before the backslash-escaping loop. It does not flatten other Unicode/ASCII line-break characters such as U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR), U+0085 (NEL), \v (vertical tab), or \f (form feed) — these pass through unescaped and unflattened, so a value containing one of them would still break the single-line/bullet-list Markdown rendering. The doc's unqualified 'line breaks flattened' is broader than what the code does (only CR/LF).

claim: AC-10: the Markdown answer in the tool result text contains the **col:** value lines and no Markdown table for a qualifying result
